• The Residential Tenancy Act, the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act and the Short-Term Rental Accommodations Act would all be repealed.
  • The new Act would apply to rental arrangements, written or oral, entered into on or after the repeal date. This includes short-term rentals.
  • The Provincial Court would hear disputes about rental arrangements, including matters the Residential Tenancy Branch could hear before the repeal.
  • The Residential Tenancy Branch could not accept new applications or start new proceedings after the repeal date.
  • The Branch would continue only to finish proceedings begun before the repeal date. Its authority would end on a date set by regulation.
  • Tenancy agreement references to the old dispute process would be treated as references to Provincial Court, except for proceedings the Branch continues.
  • Municipalities keep their power to regulate or prohibit short-term rentals and other residential use under their bylaws.
  • The government could make regulations on the short-term rental duration, rent, fees, deposits, termination, enforcement and transition. The Act starts by regulation.
4302245:
• People under 40 at the end of a tax year would pay 50% less BC income tax for that year.
  • The age test uses the person's age on the last day of the taxation year.
  • The minister must make sure total government spending drops by at least 50% within 5 years.
  • The 50% spending cut is measured against the last full fiscal year before the Act comes into force.
  • Spending means government expenditures reported through the consolidated revenue fund in the public accounts.
  • The tax cut starts on a date set by the Lieutenant Governor in Council by regulation. The rest starts at Royal Assent.
  • Section 5 of the Offence Act, which covers general offences, does not apply to this Act or its regulations.
4302246:
• A small farm is a farm with yearly gross revenue of $750,000 or less from growing plants and on-site processing. The government can set a different amount.
  • A small farming cooperative groups 2 or more small farms, up to a maximum number set by regulation. Its main purpose is farm production, processing or marketing.
  • On small farms in the Agricultural Land Reserve, the share of processed products that may come from outside the farm is cut from 50% to 25%. The rest must be produced in B.C.
  • Agri-tourism activities on small farms or cooperatives count as farm use and cannot be prohibited. Farming must stay the main use, and the activity must relate to the farm's products or practices.
  • Agri-tourism accommodation on a small farm is limited to 3 sleeping units, down from 10. Stays are capped at 120 days at a time.
  • Small farms and cooperatives must keep records proving their status. They must share these records with the minister, the Agricultural Land Commission or prescribed persons.
  • Knowingly putting false or misleading information in those records is not allowed.
  • The minister must post a food production report online by March 31 each year. It covers progress and strategies to increase B.C. food production.
4302247:
• Before the government makes a disposition of Crown land, the minister must give notice to anyone reasonably expected to be affected, money-wise or otherwise. They must also get a chance to make representations.
  • A disposition covers any government act that grants, disposes of, affects or creates rights in Crown land, or permits its use.
  • Notice must be handed to the affected person or sent by ordinary mail to their last known address.
  • By April 30 each year, the minister must prepare a report listing all Crown land that had a disposition.
  • The report must also list public money paid or received in the preceding fiscal year for Crown land dispositions, plus any other prescribed information.
  • The minister must table the report in the Legislative Assembly, or deposit it with the Clerk if the Assembly is not sitting. It must also be published on a public website.
  • A special committee of the Legislative Assembly is to be appointed at the earliest opportunity. It will examine Crown land dispositions and the public money spent on them. It will also look at an oversight authority and a compensation fund for affected persons.
  • The committee must report to the Legislative Assembly within one year of being appointed. The Cabinet can make regulations on notice content and report information.
4302248:
• Every February is proclaimed as Chinese Heritage Month in British Columbia.
  • The Act comes into force on the date of Royal Assent.
4302249:
• Practitioners could not prescribe, dispense or administer a drug in an "experimental drugs class" unless its wholesaler has signed a risk management agreement.
  • The Act itself designates four classes: COVID-19 vaccines (including mRNA) in the provincial program, and drugs used in harm reduction or safer supply programs.
  • It also designates drugs used to suppress puberty or for hormone treatment for gender transition, and SSRIs prescribed for mental health purposes.
  • The minister may designate more classes, considering things like how widely a drug is used, uncertainty about its long-term safety or effectiveness, and health system costs.
  • The agreement must require the wholesaler to set up and run a compensation fund for patients who have had, or are at material risk of, adverse health impacts.
  • The agreement must also require the wholesaler to repay the government for health care system costs linked to adverse impacts, long-term outcomes or increased use of public health services.
  • The minister may set conditions on use, including wholesaler reporting on prescribing and dispensing. The minister may also require an agreement before a drug is publicly funded.
  • The government may make regulations on the form and content of agreements. This Act would prevail over conflicting laws and start by regulation.
